questions.text: Entering the try: block implies that:
options: all of the instructions from this block will be executed
none of the instructions from this block will be executed
some of the instructions from this block may not be executed
questions.explanation: If an exception is raised partway through the try block, execution jumps immediately to the except clause - remaining instructions in the try block are skipped.

options: cannot be used if any named block has been used
questions.explanation: A bare except: catches everything, so it must come last - Python enforces this (a bare except before a named one is a SyntaxError).

questions.text: The top-most Python exception is called:
questions.explanation: BaseException sits at the root of Python's exception hierarchy, above Exception.

options: will stop the program when var != 0
will stop the program when var == 0
questions.explanation: assert raises AssertionError (halting the program) when its condition is False, i.e. when var != 0. When var == 0, it passes silently. Verified by running it - it's valid code, not erroneous.

questions.text: What is the expected output of the following code?
questions.explanation: "5" is a string literal (in quotes), so "5"/0 divides a string by an int, raising TypeError - not ArithmeticError or ZeroDivisionError. TypeError isn't a subclass of ArithmeticError, so it falls through to the bare except:, printing 'some'. Verified by running it.
questions.context:
try:
    print("5"/0)
except ArithmeticError:
    print("arith")
except ZeroDivisionError:
    print("zero")
except:
    print("some")

questions.text: Which of the following are examples of built-in concrete Python exceptions? (Select two answers)
questions.explanation: ArithmeticError is an abstract/grouping exception - it exists as a parent class (FloatingPointError, OverflowError, ZeroDivisionError all inherit from it, confirmed via __subclasses__) and is rarely raised directly. IndexError and ImportError are concrete exceptions actually raised for specific errors.

options: short for American Standard Code for Information Interchange
a form of encoding Unicode code points
the 9th version of the UTF standard
questions.explanation: UTF-8 is a variable-width encoding for Unicode code points.

options: like ASCII, but much more expansive
questions.explanation: Standard course description - Unicode extends ASCII's concept to cover vastly more characters.
'\'' is a string containing a single escaped apostrophe character - len(x) = 1. Verified by running it.
3*'abc' repeats the string three times, then 'xyz' is concatenated: 'abcabcabc' + 'xyz' = 'abcabcabcxyz'.
'Mike' is a prefix of 'Mikey', so it's lexicographically smaller (shorter prefix strings sort before longer ones that extend them). 'Mike' > 'Mikey' is False.
"1, 3" isn't a valid float string (comma and space aren't parseable) - float() raises ValueError. Verified by running it.
